question: From a point 15 m away from the base of a tree, the angle of elevation to the top is 45°. What is the height of the tree?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **angle of elevation** is **45°**, the **base** and **height** of the right-angled triangle are always **equal**.

In a 45°−45°−90° triangle, the ratio of sides is **1 : 1 : √2**.

Since the distance from the base (base) is **15 m**, the height must also be **15 m**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance from the base (BC) = **15 m**, Angle of elevation (θ) = **45°**.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular (Height) ÷ Base (Distance)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26f3c27aa26c729d179106fc8c3fdcaa1512a2c7a930a11bcf6919e61ebab388.png] 

⇒ tan 45° = Height ÷ 15

⇒ 1 = Height ÷ 15

⇒ Height = 1 × 15

⇒ Height = **15 m**

**∴ The correct answer is 15 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios at 45°

For a 45° angle, **sin 45° = 1/√2**, **cos 45° = 1/√2**, and **tan 45° = 1**.

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the **line of sight** with the **horizontal** when looking up at an object.

Special Right Triangles

In a **30°−60°−90°** triangle, the sides opposite to the angles are in the ratio **1 : √3 : 2**.</p
